questions.q: A holding company groups several subsidiaries under common ownership and shared goals. In TOGAF terms, this grouping is best classified as which of the following?
o: A single legal entity that cannot be an enterprise
An enterprise that may itself comprise multiple enterprises
questions.e: An enterprise is any collection of organizations with common goals, and an enterprise may itself comprise multiple enterprises, such as a holding company with subsidiaries.

questions.q: Which two architecture domains together are commonly referred to as the Information Systems Architectures?
questions.e: Data and Application together form the Information Systems Architectures, developed in Phase C. Data, Application, and Technology together are often called IT architecture.

questions.q: Which abstraction level answers the question 'Why is the architecture needed?'
questions.e: The four abstraction levels are Contextual (why), Conceptual (what), Logical (how), and Physical (with what). Contextual addresses environment, scope, goals, and drivers.

questions.q: Which two complementary concepts make up the Enterprise Continuum?
questions.e: The Enterprise Continuum comprises the Architecture Continuum and the Solutions Continuum, classifying assets from generic to organization-specific.

questions.q: In the Architecture Continuum, how does the enterprise move from generic to specific assets?
o: Specific industry models are made generic for one organization
Generic architectures are adapted and specialized to create organization-specific architectures
Solution building blocks are converted into principles
Baseline architectures are archived as foundation models
questions.e: Generic (industry-wide) architectures on the left are adapted to the enterprise to create the specific architecture on the right; specific architectures can also be generalized back for future reuse.

questions.q: Which part of the Architecture Repository stores the standards that new architectures must comply with?
questions.e: The Standards Library holds standards new architectures must comply with, including industry standards, supplier products, and shared services. The Reference Library holds guidelines, templates, and patterns.

questions.q: Which statement best captures the difference between the Content Framework and the Architecture Repository?
o: The Content Framework stores developed artifacts; the Repository defines them
The Content Framework defines which work products to develop; the Repository stores the developed ones
They are the same thing under two names
The Content Framework classifies assets from generic to specific
questions.e: The Content Framework describes what to develop and mirrors the ADM phases; the actual developed work products are stored in the Architecture Repository.

questions.q: When is the Enterprise Metamodel typically customized for an organization?
o: In the Preliminary Phase, as part of tailoring the framework
It is fixed by TOGAF and cannot be changed
questions.e: The Enterprise Metamodel is enterprise-specific and is customized in the Preliminary Phase as part of tailoring the framework. TOGAF does not constrain the notation used.

questions.q: In which ADM phase is the Architecture Capability first established?
questions.e: The Architecture Capability, the organization structures, roles, skills, responsibilities, and processes to do EA, is established in the Preliminary Phase. It is assessed against current needs in Phase H.

questions.q: In a gap analysis matrix, a target ABB that has no corresponding baseline ABB appears where, and signifies what?
o: In the 'eliminated' column, to be shut down
In the 'new' row, as a gap to be developed or procured
In the Requirements Repository as out of scope
questions.e: A target ABB missing from the baseline is recorded in the 'new' row as a gap to be developed or procured. The 'eliminated' column lists baseline ABBs intentionally removed.

questions.q: Which phase of the ADM develops the baseline and target Technology Architecture?
questions.e: Phase D develops the Technology Architecture. Phase B is Business, Phase C is Data and Application, and Phase E is Opportunities and Solutions.

questions.q: Once a deliverable is approved, how may it subsequently be changed?
o: It cannot change under any circumstances
Only through a change control or governance process
Freely, by any architect on the team
Only by the sponsor without review
questions.e: Approved does not mean finalized. Approved deliverables may evolve in later phases, but only through a change control or governance process.

questions.q: Which statement about the ADM is correct?
o: The steps within each phase are mandatory and fixed
The steps within each phase are recommendations, to be tailored under governance
Phases must always run strictly A through H with no overlap
The Preliminary Phase is optional for every project
questions.e: The steps within each phase are recommendations, not mandates. The ADM does not mandate a sequence or a waterfall; it is tailored to the situation under architecture governance.

questions.q: What does the ADM cycle graphic (the 'crop circle') actually represent?
o: A mandated activity sequence to follow in order
A stylized representation of essential information flows
The organizational chart of the architecture team
questions.e: The graphic is a stylized representation of essential information flows between phases, not a process model, activity sequence, or waterfall.

questions.q: With respect to Architecture Governance, what does the Preliminary Phase do?
o: Operates the governance process on live projects
Establishes the governance process, but does not operate it
questions.e: The Preliminary Phase establishes the Architecture Governance process; it does not operate it. Operation and enforcement happen later, notably in Phase G.

questions.q: Which of the following is a primary objective of Phase A?
o: Finalize the Implementation and Migration Plan
Define scope, identify stakeholders, and obtain approval to proceed
questions.e: Phase A defines scope, identifies stakeholders, creates the Architecture Vision, and obtains approval to proceed, the critical gate that ends the phase.

questions.q: Which of the following is identified during Phase E, Opportunities and Solutions?
o: Delivery vehicles such as programs, projects, and portfolios
questions.e: Phase E performs initial implementation planning and identifies delivery vehicles (programs, projects, portfolios) and Transition Architectures.

questions.q: During Phase F, how is migration planning best characterized?
o: The architect finalizes the plan alone and hands it to project managers
The detailed plan is finalized and governance transitions from developing to realizing the EA
The Architecture Vision is drafted for the first time
Compliance reviews of the implementation are conducted
questions.e: Phase F finalizes the detailed Implementation and Migration Plan and transitions governance from developing to realizing the EA; the Implementation Governance Model is created here.

questions.q: What is the primary purpose of Phase G, Implementation Governance?
o: To provide architectural oversight ensuring implementation conforms to the target
To assess organizational readiness for change
questions.e: Phase G provides architectural oversight of implementation, ensuring what is built conforms to the target architecture. TOGAF aligns with Agile in this phase.

questions.q: A Change Request in Phase H may result in which of the following?
o: Only a full new ADM cycle, never a light update
Either a light architecture update or the start of a new ADM cycle
Automatic approval of the Target Architecture
questions.e: Phase H is a holding phase; a Change Request is assessed to decide whether a light update or a full new ADM cycle is warranted.

questions.q: Requirements Management connects to every ADM phase except which one?
questions.e: Requirements Management sits at the centre and connects to every phase except the Preliminary Phase; it operates continuously throughout the cycle.

questions.q: Which task is the responsibility of the Requirements Management phase itself, rather than the ADM phases?
o: Conducting gap analysis and revising the target
Assessing the impact of a requirement change on the architecture
Operating the process and generating a Requirements Impact Statement
Prioritizing and addressing the architecture requirements
questions.e: Requirements Management operates the process, consolidates requirements, monitors the requirements baseline, and generates a Requirements Impact Statement; the actual architecture work happens in the ADM phases.

questions.q: TOGAF distinguishes two levels of principles. How do architecture principles relate to enterprise principles?
o: Enterprise principles sit below architecture principles
Architecture principles sit below enterprise principles and embody their spirit
questions.e: Enterprise principles guide decision making across the enterprise; architecture principles govern the architecture work, sit below the enterprise principles, and embody their spirit.

questions.q: In the Architecture Principles template, which section states the fundamental rule in a short, crisp form?
questions.e: The template is Name, Statement, Rationale, Implications. The Statement is the short, crisp expression of the fundamental rule.

questions.q: A principle written so that it applies without contradiction and allows balanced, flexible interpretation meets which criterion?
questions.e: Consistent means the principle allows balanced, flexible interpretation without contradictions. The five criteria are Complete, Consistent, Stable, Understandable, and Robust.

questions.q: Good business scenario outcomes should follow which characteristic set?
o: SMART: Specific, Measurable, Actionable, Realistic, Time-bound
questions.e: Business scenario outcomes should be SMART: Specific, Measurable, Actionable, Realistic, and Time-bound. Scenarios are used mainly in Phases A and B.

questions.q: In the TOGAF Standard, interoperability is defined as which of the following?
o: The ability to run on any hardware platform
The ability to share information as well as services
The reuse of solution building blocks
questions.e: Interoperability is the ability to share information as well as services. Its forms are operational/business, information, and technical; conflicts are minimized in Phase E.

questions.q: In TOGAF risk management, what is the initial level of risk?
o: The risk categorization after mitigating actions are applied
The risk categorization before any mitigation
A risk that has no possible mitigation
The most catastrophic risk in the register
questions.e: The initial level of risk is the categorization before mitigation; the residual level of risk is the categorization after mitigating actions are applied.

questions.q: TOGAF describes risk as which of the following?
o: A certain negative event that will occur
The effect of uncertainty on objectives, with a probability and an impact
Only a cyber security threat to IT systems
A deliverable produced in Phase F
questions.e: Risk is the effect of uncertainty on objectives; it is not certain and has both a probability or frequency and an impact. TOGAF draws on SABSA risk concepts.

questions.q: Where does the TOGAF Standard provide guidance on applying the ADM to specific contexts and styles?
o: In the Architecture Content document only
In the 'Applying the ADM' fundamental content document
questions.e: Guidance on adapting the ADM to a specific architecture style or context is in the 'Applying the ADM' fundamental content document, one of the three ADM-focused documents.

questions.q: Which level of the Architecture Landscape provides direction setting at the executive level with low detail over a long time horizon?
questions.e: The Strategic level is enterprise-wide, low detail, long horizon, for executive direction setting. The levels are Strategic, Segment, and Capability, not states.

questions.q: According to TOGAF, how far should an architecture be partitioned?
o: Until it mirrors the organizational chart exactly
Until each architecture has one owning team
Into exactly four partitions, one per domain
questions.e: Partition until each architecture has one owning team, which avoids unclear responsibilities. The partitioning model should reflect the enterprise operating model.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT one of the four scoping dimensions in TOGAF?
questions.e: The four scope dimensions are Breadth, Depth, Time Period, and Architecture Domain. Segment is a Landscape level, not a scope dimension.

questions.q: Architecture Governance is best described as which of the following?
o: A standalone discipline separate from corporate governance
Part of corporate governance, directing and controlling the EA enterprise-wide
A one-time review performed at the end of a project
The same activity as project management
questions.e: Architecture Governance directs and controls the EA at the enterprise level and is part of corporate governance, operating within a hierarchy of governance structures.

questions.q: Where do decision rights over the target architecture ultimately lie?
questions.e: Decision rights over the target architecture always lie with the stakeholders. The Architecture Board owns the processes and recommendations, but the architect assesses and stakeholders approve.

questions.q: Which type of Architecture Contract is the Statement of Architecture Work?
o: A contract between the architecting organization and the sponsor
A contract with system integrators and application providers
A contract between business users who build and deploy
A contract with an external auditor
questions.e: The Statement of Architecture Work is a type of Architecture Contract between the architecting organization and the sponsor, originating in Phase A.

questions.q: Which of the following describes the 'Consistent' level of architecture conformance?
o: The implementation has no features in common with the architecture
The implementation adheres to all the mandatory requirements and some recommended ones
The implementation addresses all the relevant mandatory and recommended requirements of the architecture
The implementation adheres to all mandatory and recommended requirements and has been formally certified
questions.e: 'Consistent' means the implementation addresses all relevant mandatory and recommended requirements. 'Compliant' adds formal certification. The six levels are: Irrelevant, Consistent, Compliant, Conformant, Fully Conformant, Non-conformant.

questions.q: Which statement about a viewpoint is correct?
o: A viewpoint is specific to a single architecture and cannot be reused
A viewpoint is generic and reusable, and can be stored in a viewpoint library
A viewpoint is always a matrix
A viewpoint is the same as a stakeholder concern
questions.e: A viewpoint is generic and reusable, defining conventions for constructing a view, and is stored in viewpoint libraries. A view is the specific representation built from it.

questions.q: Which of the following is a characteristic of a well-designed building block?
o: It is tightly coupled to a single implementation
It interoperates through a published, stable interface and has defined boundaries
It is defined only at the physical level
It cannot be reused across architectures
questions.e: A good building block is reusable, replaceable, well specified, loosely coupled to its implementation, and interoperates via a published, stable interface with defined boundaries.

questions.q: Which deliverable is the quantitative companion to the Architecture Definition Document, holding measurable criteria an implementation must meet?
questions.e: The Architecture Requirements Specification is the quantitative companion to the ADD, holding measurable criteria. Both the ADD and the ARS are finalized in Phase F.
